accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. National Commission for Women — NCW Act, 1990
2. National Commission for Minorities — NCM Act, 1992
3. National Human Rights Commission — Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
4. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights — Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The respective governing Acts were enacted in 1990, 1992, 1993 and 2005.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Act-year pairs and eliminate codes that omit a correct pair.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
The National Commission for Women was constituted in:

a. January 1990
b. January 1992
c. January 1993
d. January 1995
accepted.x: The National Commission for Women was constituted in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the parent Act from the year in which the body was set up.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was set up in:

a. 1978
b. 1990
c. 1992
d. 1993
accepted.x: The first statutory National Commission for Minorities was set up in 1993 under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992. A non-statutory Minorities Commission had earlier been created by a Ministry of Home Affairs resolution in 1978.
accepted.tq: Separate the earlier non-statutory body from the later statutory commission.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
The National Human Rights Commission was established on:

a. 28 September 1993
b. 12 October 1993
c. 26 November 1993
d. 10 December 1993
accepted.x: The NHRC was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. The Ordinance relating to it had been promulgated on 28 September 1993.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the date of the Ordinance and the date of establishment.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
Which one of the following bodies was set up in 2007 under a law enacted in 2005?

a. National Commission for Women
b. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
c. National Commission for Minorities
d. National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
accepted.x: The NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive Act-year and establishment-year combination to identify the body.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. The NCSC is provided for under Article 338.
2. The NCST is provided for under Article 338A.
3. The NCBC is provided for under Article 338B.
4. The National Commission for Women is provided for under Article 338C.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The NCW is a statutory body under the NCW Act, 1990 and is not established under Article 338C.
accepted.tq: Check the constitutional Article attached to each commission and reject the invented Article.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is correct?

a. The 65th Constitutional Amendment of 1990 created separate commissions for the SCs and STs.
b. The 89th Constitutional Amendment of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into the NCSC and NCST.
c. The separate commissions began functioning in 1990.
d. The NCST is established under Article 338B.
o: The 65th Constitutional Amendment of 1990 created separate commissions for the SCs and STs.
The separate commissions began functioning in 1990.
The NCST is established under Article 338B.
The 89th Constitutional Amendment of 2003 bifurcated the combined commission into the NCSC and NCST.
accepted.x: The 65th Amendment created a combined SC/ST Commission. The 89th Amendment in 2003 bifurcated it, and separate bodies functioned from 2004; the NCST is under Article 338A.
accepted.tq: Watch for swapped amendment numbers, Articles and dates in constitutional-body questions.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is NOT a statutory body under the Ministry of Women and Child Development?

a. National Commission for Women
b. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
c. Central Adoption Resource Authority
d. National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
accepted.x: NCW, NCPCR and CARA are the three statutory bodies under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The NCSK is under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and is non-statutory since 2004.
accepted.tq: Find the body belonging to the neighbouring ministry and different legal category.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements regarding linguistic minorities is correct?

a. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
b. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
c. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the NCBC under Article 338B.
d. Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Women.
o: Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Women.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992.
Linguistic minorities are dealt with by the NCBC under Article 338B.
accepted.x: Linguistic minorities do not fall under the National Commission for Minorities. They fall under the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities provided under Article 350B.
accepted.tq: Separate religious-minority institutions from the constitutional protection for linguistic minorities.
accepted.sec: Statutory body → Act and year (NHRC, NCW, NCM, NCPCR, NCSK)

accepted.s:
The National Commission for Women consists of:

a. A Chairperson, three Members and a Member-Secretary
b. A Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary
c. A Chairperson, seven Members and a Secretary-General
d. Five Members and a Secretary appointed by Parliament
o: A Chairperson, seven Members and a Secretary-General
A Chairperson, three Members and a Member-Secretary
Five Members and a Secretary appointed by Parliament
A Chairperson, five Members and a Member-Secretary
accepted.x: The NCW comprises one Chairperson, five Members and one Member-Secretary. All are nominated by the Central Government.
accepted.tq: Use the exact composition and do not confuse nomination with election or parliamentary appointment.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
Who nominates the Chairperson, Members and Member-Secretary of the National Commission for Women?

a. The President of India
b. The Parliament
c. The Central Government
d. The Supreme Court of India
accepted.x: The Chairperson, five Members and Member-Secretary of the NCW are nominated by the Central Government.
accepted.tq: Apply the “who would do this job?” method to distinguish nomination from constitutional appointment.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women?

a. Jayanti Patnaik
b. Vijaya Rahatkar
c. Mohini Giri
d. Girija Vyas
accepted.x: Jayanti Patnaik was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Women.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from later chairpersons and other prominent office-holders.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is NOT a function of the National Commission for Women?

a. Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
b. Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
c. Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
d. Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
o: Suggesting amendments to laws affecting women
Taking suo motu notice where women’s rights are denied
Commissioning special studies on discrimination and atrocities against women
Enforcing criminal sentences imposed by courts
accepted.x: The NCW may review laws, suggest amendments, take suo motu notice and commission special studies. It does not enforce criminal sentences imposed by courts.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that converts a recommendatory statutory function into a coercive judicial power.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Women:

1. The Central Government must consult it on all major policy matters affecting women.
2. It may appoint committees for particular purposes.
3. It may co-opt persons from outside the Commission.
4. It has no power to regulate its own procedure.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The NCW may regulate its own procedure, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the negative statement that reverses an expressly stated procedural power.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
In the context of women’s rights, a ‘Jan Sunwai’ refers to:

a. A closed-door meeting of judges
b. A public hearing of women’s grievances
c. An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
d. A legislative session on gender budgeting
o: A public hearing of women’s grievances
A legislative session on gender budgeting
An annual financial audit of women’s commissions
accepted.x: Jan Sunwai refers to public hearings conducted to hear and address women’s grievances.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a programme term rather than its broad policy context.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
The five-day Jan Sunwai conducted by the Andhra Pradesh Mahila Commission in March 2026 was held during:

a. 1–5 March 2026
b. 9–13 March 2026
c. 15–19 March 2026
d. 20–24 March 2026
accepted.x: The five-day Jan Sunwai was held from 9 to 13 March 2026 in five zones, including Nellore, Guntur, Vijayawada and Rajamahendravaram, on directions from the NCW.
accepted.tq: Use the exact date range and distinguish it from nearby five-day alternatives.
accepted.sec: NCW - NCW Act 1990, composition, functions (Section 10), first chairperson, Jan Sunwai

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis?

a. Act lapsed — 1998
b. Change to non-statutory status — 2004
c. Ministry — Women and Child Development
d. Governing Act currently in force — NCSK Act, 1993
o: Governing Act currently in force — NCSK Act, 1993
accepted.x: The NCSK Act, 1993 lapsed in 2004, after which the NCSK continued as a non-statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The Act is not currently in force as its governing basis.
accepted.tq: Separate the original statutory status from the present non-statutory status.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

accepted.s:
The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis is presently continued primarily through:

a. Constitutional provision under Article 338D
b. Periodic tenure extensions by government resolution
c. Annual elections conducted by sanitation workers
d. Orders of the Supreme Court alone
o: Orders of the Supreme Court alone
Periodic tenure extensions by government resolution
Annual elections conducted by sanitation workers
accepted.x: After the NCSK Act lapsed in 2004, the Commission continued as a non-statutory body through periodic tenure extensions by government resolution.
accepted.tq: Apply the legal-status distinction to determine the present institutional basis.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

accepted.s:
In January 2022, the Union Cabinet extended the tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis for:

a. One year beyond 31 March 2022
b. Two years beyond 31 March 2022
c. Three years beyond 31 March 2022
d. Five years beyond 31 March 2022
accepted.x: In January 2022, the Union Cabinet extended the NCSK for three years beyond 31 March 2022, taking the tenure up to 31 March 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the extension period with its terminal date rather than relying on the Act’s original year.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

accepted.s:
The tenure of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis was subsequently extended up to:

a. 31 March 2026
b. 31 March 2027
c. 31 March 2028
d. 31 December 2028
accepted.x: After the extension up to 31 March 2025, the NCSK received a further three-year extension up to 31 March 2028.
accepted.tq: Track successive tenure extensions chronologically and identify the final date.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

accepted.s:
Which of the following functions is associated with the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis?

a. Monitoring the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reporting to the Government
b. Conducting the census of all urban households
c. Appointing municipal commissioners in every State
d. Issuing constitutional amendments concerning sanitation
o: Appointing municipal commissioners in every State
Conducting the census of all urban households
Monitoring the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reporting to the Government
accepted.x: The NCSK monitors implementation of the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers Act, 2013 and reports to the Government.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that states a monitoring and reporting responsibility rather than an unrelated executive power.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

accepted.s:
The missed-call grievance line for sanitation workers was launched on the foundation day of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis, observed on:

a. 15 August
b. 23 August
c. 2 October
d. 26 November
accepted.x: The missed-call grievance line was launched on the NCSK’s foundation day, 23 August 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive institutional date instead of confusing it with national observance days.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

accepted.s:
Who among the following was the Vice-Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis as reported in 2026?

a. Hardeep Singh Gill
b. Jayanti Patnaik
c. Vijaya Rahatkar
d. Santosh Hegde
accepted.x: Hardeep Singh Gill was the Vice-Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis as reported in 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the office-holder with the correct statutory body and avoid swapping names across commissions.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

a. NAMASTE — 2022; associated with NSKFDC
b. Jan Sunwai — appointment of NCSK Vice-Chairperson
c. NCSK Act — constitutional provision under Article 338A
d. Article 350B — National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: Jan Sunwai — appointment of NCSK Vice-Chairperson
NCSK Act — constitutional provision under Article 338A
Article 350B — National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
accepted.x: NAMASTE is associated with the NSKFDC and dates from 2022. Jan Sunwai concerns public hearings of women’s grievances, Article 338A concerns the NCST, and Article 350B concerns linguistic minorities.
accepted.tq: Use nearby institutional facts to catch swapped bodies, Articles and programmes.
accepted.sec: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis - legal status, tenure extensions
